clue.text: Like Canute's race to secure popular backing?

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it within, so the dash wraps the reversed piece

parts.note: to race is to dash

indicators.note: backing says the word for popular is turned round

parts.note: in means popular, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A question whether King Canute's people managed to win public support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' and 'to secure' do the work; 'race' is a dash, not a people. Canute (Cnut) was an 11th-century king of Denmark as well as England.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was a Dane, so anything like his nation or people is described by the adjective for Denmark.

clue.text: Woman's strong dislike for compound

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so Di's
odium is hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: A woman's intense aversion to some mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt containing two sodium atoms per molecule, such as disodium phosphate, is a compound.

clue.text: Token loan arranged to enclose most of pit

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the shortened pit
arranged says the letters of loan are put in a new order
most of says the pit word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A token loan set up to cover most of a coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives NOAL, 'most of' trims the pit word, and 'to enclose' wraps one round the other. 'Token' looks like a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum is a token one, very small compared with the real value.

clue.text: Soldiers using new range in groups

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the groups word

parts.note: sets are groups

indicators.note: new says the letters of range are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Soldiers using a new firing range in squads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives ERGEAN, and 'in' places it after the first two letters of the groups word; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-commissioned officers in the army are soldiers of this rank.

clue.text: Purchase drink, having left for Belgian capital

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it, so left replaces the capital letter

parts.note: any drink is a beverage

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone buys a drink after leaving Brussels behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgian capital' looks like Brussels, but it is just B, the first letter of 'Belgian'; 'having left for' it puts L in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in the sense of a firm grip or mechanical advantage is the force gained by using a lever.

clue.text: Respected politician's condition accepted by presbyter's staff

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the elder's word holds the condition

parts.note: a presbyter is an elder of the church, so presbyter's is elder's
a state is a condition
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A respected politician's health is welcomed by a church elder's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'politician's' is read as 'politician has'. 'accepted by' signals the containment. 'staff' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning to provide people for.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior figure honoured for long political service and wisdom is given this title.

clue.text: Have limited intelligence, sacrificing ends for moral principles

definitions.note: a singular noun for a set of moral principles

indicators.note: sacrificing ends says the phrase gives up its first and last letters

parts.note: to be thick is to be stupid

explanation.surface: Being dim and losing out on scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing ends' drops the B and K of BE THICK.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is the code of moral values a person or group lives by.

clue.text: Appearance of a Republican challenger

parts.note: a rival is a challenger

explanation.surface: A Republican challenger turns up in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming on the scene, or showing up, is an arrival.

clue.text: Complete set of books written in the country

indicators.note: written in says the books are placed inside the country

parts.note: Eire is Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of books composed in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' signals containment; 'set of books' is the usual crossword shorthand for one Testament of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire is whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Prohibitionist had row about English paper's screamer

parts.note: one who bans things is a banner

indicators.note: about means around, so had wraps the letter for English

parts.note: taken as written
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A prohibitionist rowed over an English newspaper's sensational story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prohibitionist' looks like a temperance campaigner; it is just one who bans. 'about' puts E inside HAD, and 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A large headline running across a front page; a screamer is slang for such a sensational headline.

clue.text: French writer having an impact in Uzbek city

indicators.note: having here means holding inside, so the writer's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
to make a mark is to have an impact

explanation.surface: A French author makes a splash in a city of Uzbekistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is the containment signal, holding the impact phrase inside the writer's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Silk Road city is one of the best-known places in Uzbekistan, famous for its mosques and madrasas.

clue.text: Injury keeping son in wood

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the injury word wraps the letter for son

parts.note: a hurt is an injury
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy is hurt while out in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts S inside HURT.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a wooded hillock or copse, surviving in English place names.

clue.text: Place of confinement debt collector has no say about

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of a debt

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the words for no and say are read backwards

parts.note: say means 'for example', abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A debt collector without any voice in the matter, trapped somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the two short words to make GEON. 'say' is not speech here but 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in which prisoners were confined.

clue.text: Get better play area completed

parts.note: the rec is the recreation ground, a British public playing field
something completed is over

explanation.surface: Recovering health after a playground has been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rec' (recreation ground) is a British local park for games.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health after illness, which is getting better.

clue.text: Old cavalryman retreating in exceptional humiliation

indicators.note: retreating says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former horse soldier withdraws in great shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters NALHU hidden across 'exceptional humiliation', and 'retreating' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer in the Polish, Prussian or Austrian light cavalry of past centuries.

clue.text: Art school board accepts first of etchings, subject to evaluation

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Academy of Arts in London, runs schools of art

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the table holds the letter

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'bed and board'

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of etchings

explanation.surface: An art school's governing board takes in some etchings for appraisal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts E inside TABLE. 'board' is not a governing body here but a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that can be assessed for local rates, a British property tax, is open to valuation.

clue.text: A switch between opposing sides in port

indicators.note: between says the switch word sits within the two sides

parts.note: right and left, R and L, are opposite sides
to switch is to change

explanation.surface: A change of allegiance between opposing parties in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts CHANGE between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkhangelsk is a Russian port on the White Sea, known in English by this name.

clue.text: Subject to bet, it could be inferior to Axminster

definitions.text: it could be inferior to Axminster

parts.note: under means subject to, as in 'under orders'
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: Something lesser than a fine Axminster carpet, open to a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a British make of woven carpet; 'inferior' here means lying beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding laid beneath a carpet sits physically lower than it, so is inferior in the positional sense.

clue.text: Street clubs not long established around south

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the recent word goes around the letter for south

parts.note: something not long established is recent

explanation.surface: Clubs on a street that only opened recently, somewhere in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S inside RECENT. 'Street' is the definition, a common British road name.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved street of houses is often called this, as in Royal Crescent in Bath.

clue.text: Burden match official with announcement of rule

parts.note: ref is short for referee

indicators.note: announcement of means the word for rule is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: Loading a referee with a ruling to proclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a load, but it also means the chorus of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is an old word for the repeated chorus of a song, which is a refrain.

clue.text: Most of capital knight put together for monument

indicators.note: most of says the capital's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Cairo is the capital of Egypt
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Much of a capital city and a knight combined to build a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims CAIRO to CAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of stones raised as a memorial or landmark.

clue.text: Big fire I observed primarily consuming northern plant

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so I and O enclose the other pieces
primarily picks the first letter of observed

parts.note: a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A blaze watched first-hand as it devours a northern plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts N FERN between I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, raging fire.

clue.text: Way in which old Liberals must enter valley

indicators.note: must enter says these letters go inside the way word

parts.note: how means the way in which
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Old Liberal politicians are obliged to come into a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must enter' signals containment; 'Way in which' as a unit means how, not a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a small valley or dip in the ground.

clue.text: Casual worker following start of race

indicators.note: following says the worker comes after the start

parts.note: the off is the start of a horse race
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A temporary worker trails behind at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of race' looks like an instruction to take R; it is the off, the start of a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual, careless and without much thought.

clue.text: Appearing in drag: a military trumpeter

indicators.note: appearing in says the answer shows itself within the following words

explanation.surface: A military bugler turning up in women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpeter' looks like a bugler but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The agami is a South American bird also called the trumpeter for its loud call.

clue.text: Second French article whose content is inferior? A bit

parts.note: naff is British slang for cheap or inferior
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A second-rate French magazine piece, questioned as only a fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: The inferior word, British slang for tacky, is the article's content, so it comes before the article. 'A bit' looks like 'a little', but it is a horse's bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse's bridle is a type of bit.

clue.text: A device for fastening back climbing plant

indicators.note: back says the letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a nail is used to fasten things together

explanation.surface: A clip to fasten back a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses A NAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up tree trunks.

clue.text: Speech made by new president during month by Russian river

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in June'
Aug is the abbreviation for August
the Ural flows from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A newly elected president speaks at some point in the month, near a Russian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'president'; 'by' then links to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The first address given on taking office is the opening, or inaugural, one.

clue.text: Girl Guide leader touring quiet place in Canada

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the girl's name goes around the letter for quiet

parts.note: Winnie is a girl's name
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide leader on tour around a peaceful spot in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guide leader' reads as one person; split it into Girl (WINNIE) and Guide leader (G). 'touring' puts P inside WINNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Canadian province of Manitoba.

clue.text: Like goo finally slithering round the bend

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of slithering

parts.note: round the bend is British slang for crazy, which is loopy

explanation.surface: Something gooey ends up sliding around a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like a road; it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloop is a thick, sticky substance, so something gloopy has a gooey texture.
